title: ksm-control-daemon vs ksmtuned installation (Proxmox forum; one of several forum results)
supports: (via search snippet) Proxmox forum users report ksmtuned is enabled by default on ISO installs and starts merging at ~80% host memory use because KSM_THRES_COEF=20 in /etc/ksmtuned.conf; Debian-based installs may lack ksm; official wiki wording not confirmed. Supports RT-HYP-DD4-02 / RT-VC-DD4-03 / RT-VET-DD4-02 acceptance

title: ksm is needlessly burning cpu because of using vzs and ignoring arcsize (Proxmox forum)
supports: (via search snippet) ksmtuned keys off VSZ not RSS and ignores ZFS ARC, so KSM can run even at low thresholds on Proxmox hosts: KSM is commonly active on stock Proxmox

title: [RFC PATCH v2] zswap: memcontrol: implement zswap writeback disabling
supports: (via search snippet) writing 0 to a cgroup's memory.zswap.writeback disables zswap writeback to the backing swap device for that cgroup; default 1. Basis for the zswap-only (no SSD writeback) policy answering RT-PHY-DD4-05

title: [PATCH v2 1/2] mm/memcontrol: respect zswap.writeback setting from parent cg too
supports: (via search snippet) in kernels before this 2024 fix memory.zswap.writeback was not hierarchical: disabling at a parent left child cgroups writing back; the agent must set it per leaf cgroup on older kernels

title: hwpoison (Linux kernel documentation, mm)
supports: (via search snippet) memory-failure recovery handles only LRU pages; most kernel internal objects cannot be recovered; vm.memory_failure_recovery=0 panics on any failure. Supports RT-PHY-DD4-06: a UE in the kernel-owned zswap/zsmalloc pool is generally not recoverable

title: Re: [PATCH] zswap: do not crash the kernel on decompression failure
supports: (via search snippet) zswap previously crashed the kernel on decompression failure (memory corruption or compressor bug); the proposal SIGBUSes only the loading process; merge status not confirmed. Covers detected corruption, not MCE consumption in kernel context
